standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a prime divisor, of a dimension function, and the local shape of an effective Cartier divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, labels divisors-definition-Weil-divisor (proof line 2508), divisors-lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points (proof line 2515); Topology, label topology-definition-dimension-function (proof line 2510); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-one-equation (proof line 2518); Properties, label properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring (proof line 2519)
standard_prerequisites.use: The definitions give part (1); for part (2) the local equation of the divisor and the one-equation lemma give that the local ring at the generic point has dimension one, whence the dimension function drops by one.

core_obligations: Part (1) follows directly from the definitions of a prime divisor and of a dimension function (proof lines 2506-2510).

Part (2): let the point be the generic point of an irreducible component of the effective Cartier divisor, note that the local ring of the divisor there has dimension zero and is the quotient of the local ring of the ambient scheme by a nonzerodivisor, so the ambient local ring has dimension one (proof lines 2511-2517).
Conclude that the component has the expected dimension by the dimension formula for local rings (proof lines 2518-2520).
proof_roadmap: Local equation and dimension one (proof lines 2511-2517).
Conclusion via the local ring dimension formula (proof lines 2518-2520).
difficulty_reason: The lemma translates the notions of prime divisor and of the components of an effective Cartier divisor into statements about the relative dimension function (statement lines 2488-2504, tag 02RE-adjacent). Part (1) is definitional, while part (2) requires the local analysis of an effective Cartier divisor at the generic point of a component, where the local ring of the divisor is the quotient of the ambient local ring by a nonzerodivisor, so the ambient ring has dimension one. That local argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
